resumo: EU leaders left Brussels without agreement on the budget to 2034; in Portugal, the State Budget war heads for an urgent debate on 3 December; FIFA and the AFP news agency confirm cyberattacks; and Europe's Euclid telescope finds the oldest quasar ever.

noticias.titulo: FIFA confirms cyberattack: hackers reached «a limited set» of personal and business data
noticias.estado: Attack confirmed by FIFA · scale and perpetrators unclear · group's claim not confirmed
texto: FIFA, the body that runs world football, has been hit by a cyberattack. The federation itself, based in Zurich, Switzerland, confirmed it on Thursday 26 November: someone gained unauthorised access to «a limited set» of personal and business information. FIFA says it is working with the authorities, including the police, and condemns the illegal obtaining and publication of the data.

What we know — and what we don't. FIFA did not say when the attack happened, how many people or partners were affected, or what kind of documents were taken. A source close to the matter told Reuters that less than 0.1% of the organisation's total information was hit, and that the files on the abandoned plan to sell a stake in the tournaments to private investors were not touched.

Last week, a group calling itself the Handsome Boy Hacking Club posted on X an image it said showed internal FIFA files. Three days later, according to AP, it appeared to claim the attack when replying to a post about the leak of more than 12 gigabytes of documents. FIFA has not commented on that claim.

The case comes at a delicate time for the federation. Gianni Infantino, president for 11 years, is standing for a new term running to 2031 in the election set for 18 March, against Japan's Kohzo Tashima and France's Philippe Diallo.

verificacao.nota: The confirmation of the attack and FIFA's statements match across AP (via SecurityWeek), Fox Business (with Reuters) and ECO (which cites the BBC and Reuters). The figure of less than 0.1% and the assurance that the «FIFA Forward Enterprise» plan files were not accessed come only from an anonymous source quoted by Reuters. The group's claim and the 12 GB come from AP; they have not been confirmed by FIFA. Image: the file appears in Commons search results, but its page could not be opened; what it shows is inferred from the file name.

noticias.titulo: Agence France-Presse attacked: the platform where newspapers get their stories, photos and videos is offline
noticias.estado: Attack confirmed by AFP · perpetrators unknown · no confirmation of data theft
texto: AFP (Agence France-Presse), one of the world's three big news agencies, was hit by a cyberattack in the early hours of Thursday 26 November, at around 1:30 Paris time. The target was AFP Forum, the portal where client media outlets download dispatches, photos and videos. The agency took the platform offline as a precaution and set up alternatives so clients could keep receiving content, according to an internal message from management quoted by the French press.

«At this stage, we have no information about the identity of the perpetrators», management says. AFP is analysing the case with outside experts. It has not said how the hackers got in, nor whether data was stolen or «ransomware» (software that locks systems and demands a ransom) was involved. There is also no date for the portal's return.

It is not the first time. In September 2024, AFP suffered an attack that affected systems for sending content to clients. Nothing links the two cases so far. The agency has around 1,840 journalists in 210 bureaux and produces, on average, 2,300 dispatches, 3,000 photos and 300 videos a day, in six languages.

verificacao.nota: The time of the attack, the isolation of AFP Forum, the workarounds and management's statement match in Le Monde Informatique (which cites an internal message reported by Clubic) and Génération NT (which cites Le Figaro). We were unable to read a public statement from AFP itself. Le Monde Informatique notes that the metadata of one of the sources points to the night of 25 to 26 November.

noticias.titulo: Guadeloupe's largest hospital works on paper after cyberattack; surgeries and cancer treatments postponed
noticias.estado: Attack confirmed · «ransomware» is the French cybersecurity agency's working hypothesis · no date for a return to normal
texto: The University Hospital Centre of Guadeloupe, the largest hospital in this French Caribbean territory (and therefore part of the European Union), has been running on pen and paper since the weekend. A cyberattack encrypted its databases, according to the hospital, and forced it to shut down its systems. ANSSI, the French cybersecurity agency, is investigating and points to «ransomware», software that makes data unreadable in order to demand a ransom.

The consequences are serious. Surgeries, appointments and imaging scans have been cancelled at least until Friday, radiotherapy has been suspended for safety reasons and some chemotherapy sessions were cancelled, according to The Record. A&E, dialysis and urgent cardiac cases are continuing. Test results are printed and delivered by hand, and patients have been asked to bring paper copies of their records. The hospital has activated its emergency plan (the «plan blanc», or «white plan»).

The hospital says it has not received a ransom demand and would not pay one. It is not yet known whether personal or medical data was stolen. ANSSI is trying to establish whether the attackers got in through an IT supplier, which is thought to have been compromised months earlier, and the Paris public prosecutor's office has opened an inquiry.

How long will it last? The French health minister, Stéphanie Rist, spoke of «a few days at the very least, perhaps several weeks», according to Outremers360. The hospital serves around 380,000 people.

verificacao.nota: Manual operation, the white plan and the ransomware hypothesis match in The Record and Outremers360. The details on radiotherapy, chemotherapy, the IT supplier, the Paris inquiry and the absence of a ransom demand come only from The Record. The minister's quote comes from Outremers360. The sources differ on when it began (Saturday night in The Record, Sunday in Outremers360); we used «the weekend». Developments after 25 November have not been confirmed.

fontes.nome: The Record – «Suspected ransomware attack disrupts cancer treatments, surgeries at Guadeloupe hospital» (25 Nov)
Outremers360 – «CHU de Guadeloupe: le calendrier de retour à la normale encore flou» (Guadeloupe University Hospital: timetable for return to normal still unclear) (25 Nov)

noticias.titulo: Portuguese government grants «national strategic interest» status to Portugal's bid for a European AI gigafactory
noticias.estado: Resolution approved · grid connection only if Portugal wins · European call postponed to 30 December
texto: The Council of Ministers (Portugal's cabinet) approved on Thursday 26 November a resolution recognising the «national strategic interest» of Portugal's bid for an artificial intelligence (AI) gigafactory — a giant computing centre for training and running AI models. In practice, the government guarantees that the facility will be able to connect to the public electricity grid with a capacity of up to 260 MVA (megavolt-amperes), but only if Portugal wins the European competition.

Why does this matter? The competition is run by EuroHPC, the European joint undertaking for supercomputing, co-funded by the European Commission. The idea is to create up to seven gigafactories in Europe, each with up to 100,000 latest-generation processors. Bidders must prove they can secure enough electricity, and explain the impact of cooling on water and energy consumption.

According to the EFE news agency, the state authorised in July up to €200 million, between 2027 and 2033, to buy computing time; EuroHPC would match that sum in a first phase, and total investment in the Portuguese part would be around €4 billion, with private capital. Preparations are in the hands of the Banco Português de Fomento (Portugal's state-owned development bank), and the government is negotiating with Spain over a joint Iberian bid. No location has been given.

The timetable keeps slipping. The batch in which Portugal is competing had already been moved to early December and, on 25 November, was postponed again to 30 December, according to ECO. European Commissioner Henna Virkkunen called the delays «very regrettable».

verificacao.nota: The resolution, the 260 MVA, the seven gigafactories and the role of the Banco Português de Fomento match in ECO, EFE (via Infobae) and PressNET. The €200 million, EuroHPC's matching funds and the roughly €4 billion come only from EFE. The postponement to 30 December and Henna Virkkunen's words come from ECO (which cites EuroHPC); PressNET confirms the new postponement. We did not read the Council of Ministers' statement.

PressNET – «Conselho de Ministros reconhece interesse estratégico nacional da candidatura portuguesa a uma gigafábrica de IA» (Council of Ministers recognises national strategic interest of Portugal's AI gigafactory bid) (26 Nov)

noticias.titulo: Meta's AI camera glasses in court in the Netherlands: three groups want them changed or banned
noticias.estado: Hearing held · requests from the groups · judge's ruling expected by 24 December
texto: Meta's smart glasses, which record video and sound and come with an AI assistant, went to court in Amsterdam on Thursday 26 November. Three Dutch organisations — the consumer association Consumentenbond, Offlimits (which tackles online abuse) and The Firewall — accuse Meta of breaching the GDPR, the EU's data protection regulation, and have asked for urgent measures in summary proceedings.

Their requests are not the same. Offlimits and The Firewall want sales banned, believing that is the only way to solve the problem. Consumentenbond is asking Meta to take steps against covert recording and to stop using the footage captured to train its AI models. «Our democratic society is threatened when everyone has to fear, at all times, that they are being filmed», said Offlimits' lawyer, quoted by AFP.

Meta argues that responsibility lies with the people wearing the glasses, that they only record when the user asks them to, and that a light shows when recording is under way. It also pointed out that other brands sell similar products and that the glasses help people with visual impairments. The judge will rule by 24 December, according to AG Connect.

verificacao.nota: The three groups, the Amsterdam court and the date of the hearing match in Villamedia, AG Connect and an AFP dispatch (published by the Brazilian newspaper O Povo). The difference between the requests and the date of the ruling come from AG Connect. The lawyer's quote comes from AFP (in a Brazilian Portuguese translation, adapted). Meta's arguments combine what Villamedia, AG Connect and AFP report.

fontes.nome: AG Connect – «Drie organisaties verenigd bij de rechtbank tegen gluurbril» (Three organisations united in court against «peeping glasses») (27 Nov)
Villamedia – «Meta in rechtszaal: gebruikers AI-brillen zelf verantwoordelijk» (Meta in court: AI glasses users responsible themselves) (26 Nov)
O Povo / AFP – «Várias associações holandesas pedem a proibição da venda de óculos inteligentes da Meta» (Several Dutch associations call for a ban on sales of Meta's smart glasses) (26 Nov)

noticias.titulo: Bank of England warns: the money borrowed for the AI race is increasingly «complex, circular and opaque»
noticias.estado: Official Bank of England assessment · the risks described are warnings, not crisis forecasts
texto: The Bank of England thinks the way artificial intelligence (AI) is being financed could become a problem for the financial system. In its financial stability report, published on Thursday 26 November, it describes the financing of data centres as «increasingly complex, circular and opaque», which increases the links between companies and markets and makes contagion easier if something goes wrong.

At the centre are the so-called «hyperscalers», the small group of tech giants building the big data centres. According to Reuters, they will issue more than $305 billion in debt this year, more than most governments, including the British one. According to Bloomberg, the central bank estimates these companies' total exposure to AI at more than $4 trillion, also counting commitments that sit off their balance sheets. Those commitments could come under pressure if expectations of AI profits are revised down, the bank warns.

Even after recent falls, stock market valuations remain «stretched», the report says. The bank also urges banks not to depend on a single cloud provider, after recent outages at Microsoft and Google, and wants them to switch to cryptography that can resist future quantum computers: priority systems by the end of 2031, the rest by 2035.

verificacao.nota: The description of the financing, the risk of contagion and the «stretched» valuations match in Reuters (via Global Banking & Finance Review) and Bloomberg (via Business Standard). The more than $305 billion and the post-quantum cryptography deadlines come from Reuters; the more than $4 trillion comes from Bloomberg. We did not read the Bank of England's original report.

fontes.nome: Reuters (via Global Banking & Finance Review) – «Bank of England sees growing financial risks from AI borrowing» (26 Nov)
Bloomberg (via Business Standard) – «AI firms' $4 trillion exposure amplifies global market risks: BOE» (26 Nov)

noticias.titulo: Volvo starts training humanoid robots at its Ghent plant to take the heaviest tasks off workers
noticias.estado: Training under way · pilot planned for the first half of 2027 · real production use only from mid-2027
texto: Volvo Cars is training humanoid robots at its plant in Ghent, Belgium, the first in the group to test them. The carmaker announced it on Thursday 26 November. The robots, called AEON, are made by Hexagon Robotics, a Swedish company, and learn by imitating what workers show them. Their first task is to place parts into two fixtures with great precision.

The AEON robots are 1.65 metres tall, weigh 60 kilos, move on wheels rather than legs and carry up to 10 kilos — enough for small parts, not for heavy components. The aim, Volvo says, is for them to do some of the most repetitive and physically demanding work, alongside the teams and machines already there.

The timetable is cautious: a pilot at the plant in the first half of 2027, with more robots, and use in real production from mid-2027. Tech Times notes that Volvo has not revealed how many robots it has, nor how often they need human help, and points out that the carmaker announced around 2,500 job cuts worldwide in October.

verificacao.nota: The facts about the training, the robot's specifications and the timetable come from Volvo Cars' press release and are confirmed by Tech Times. The open questions and the job cuts announced in October come only from Tech Times.

fontes.nome: Volvo Cars (press release) – «Volvo Cars trains Hexagon Robotics' humanoids for manufacturing» (26 Nov)
Tech Times – «Volvo Humanoid Robots Begin Ghent Training With One Task: Placing Parts Into Two Fixtures» (27 Nov)

noticias.titulo: Nvidia has reportedly halted shipments of AI servers to four South-East Asian countries because of new US rules
noticias.estado: Financial Times report based on anonymous sources · Nvidia has not commented · unclear whether it is temporary
texto: Nvidia has reportedly asked the manufacturers that build servers with its AI chips to stop shipping them to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia. The report is from the Financial Times, published on Thursday 26 November, based on unnamed sources: companies such as Dell and Supermicro are said to have told customers in those countries that Nvidia was not authorising the orders.

Why? Last week, the US approved rules to stop Chinese companies getting round export restrictions by renting computing power in data centres in other countries. Cloud service providers have 90 days to apply for a licence and show that they do not serve banned customers. «There's a new rule, but no guidance on how to apply it», an industry figure told the newspaper.

It is not known whether the suspension is temporary. Nvidia has made no public comment, according to the sources consulted. The region has become important for the company: its Singapore subsidiary recorded $104 billion in revenue in 2025, although that figure also includes sales to Taiwan and China, according to The National.

verificacao.nota: All the information about the suspension comes from the Financial Times (not read directly), as reported by The National and Tom's Hardware (via Yahoo Finance), which offer no confirmation of their own. The industry figure's quote and the 90-day deadline appear in both. The Singapore subsidiary figures come from The National.

fontes.nome: The National – «Nvidia halts chip shipments to South-East Asia amid US crackdown» (26 Nov)

noticias.titulo: EU summit ends without a deal on the budget to 2034 after almost 15 hours; Spain's Hernández de Cos is the pick for the ECB
noticias.estado: No budget deal (fact) · new attempt expected in mid-December · ECB: political choice, to be formalised in December
texto: The 27 leaders of the European Union (EU) failed to agree on the long-term budget for 2028–2034. The extraordinary summit in Brussels ended in the early hours of this Friday 27 November, after almost 15 hours of discussion, according to Jornal de Negócios and EUalive. The second day, planned for today, was cancelled. «We did not reach an agreement on the overall size of the budget», admitted the President of the European Council, António Costa, who called the meeting «a necessary stage in the process» and is now looking to the mid-December summit.

On the table was Costa's compromise proposal: around €1.78 trillion, below the almost €1.98 trillion proposed by the European Commission. For some it is too much, for others too little. Seven countries that pay in more than they get back, among them Germany, the Netherlands and Sweden, want bigger cuts and refused to take part in the small-group meetings Costa organised, according to Euronews. German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said further cuts will be needed. On the other side, French President Emmanuel Macron called the cuts a «strategic mistake» and warned that, without a deal by 31 December, the negotiations cannot be reopened. Italy's Giorgia Meloni said a deal is «light years» away.

And Portugal? Prime Minister Luís Montenegro said Costa's proposal is «still not enough» and that Portugal will not back it without guarantees for the cohesion funds, aimed at the poorest regions, and for the Azores and Madeira, according to Observador. The proposal gives Portugal €34.9 billion, around €400 million less than earlier versions. The €45 billion loan to Ukraine for 2027 took a back seat: Bulgaria secured an opt-out from the military part, and Hungary, Slovakia and the Czech Republic still refuse to take part, according to EUalive.

There was one decision: the leaders of the euro countries backed Spain's Pablo Hernández de Cos, former governor of the Bank of Spain, to succeed Christine Lagarde as president of the European Central Bank (ECB), according to Lusa (Portugal's news agency) and Euronews. Lagarde leaves on 7 February 2027. France's Laurence Boone and Germany's Markus Brunnermeier were put forward for other seats on the bank's board. The appointment still has to be formalised, which is expected to happen in December.

verificacao.nota: The end of the summit without a deal, the almost 15 hours, Costa's statements and the mid-December summit confirmed in Jornal de Negócios (27 Nov) and EUalive (27 Nov). The boycott by the seven «frugals» and the statements by Merz, Macron and Meloni in Euronews and EUalive. Montenegro and the sum for Portugal come from Observador (Lusa, 26 Nov). Bulgaria's position and the three countries refusing the Ukraine loan only in EUalive. The choice of Hernández de Cos, Boone and Brunnermeier in Lusa (via Correio da Manhã) and EUalive; the Euronews headline on the subject appeared in search results, but the page was not opened. The exact date of the December summit was not confirmed today (earlier sources gave 17–18 Dec). noticias.titulo: Drone attack in Kuwait kills two Italian technicians; Kuwait blames Iran, which denies it
noticias.estado: Deaths confirmed by Kuwait and Italy · Iranian responsibility: an accusation by Kuwait, denied by Tehran
texto: Two Italian technicians died on Thursday 26 November in a drone attack on a facility in Kuwait. According to Kuwait's Ministry of Defence, quoted by ABC News and Gulf News, the drones were Iranian and hit a “vital site”. Four people were wounded by shrapnel: the two Italians, who later died, a Pakistani and a Kuwaiti. Iran denies any involvement.

Italy's Foreign Ministry confirmed that the victims worked for Rheinmetall Italia, a subsidiary of the German arms group, and were maintaining an air defence system, according to Gulf News. The prime minister, Giorgia Meloni, offered her condolences to the families. The President of the European Commission, Ursula von der Leyen, called the attack “Iranian” and called for more pressure on Tehran.

On the Iranian side, the armed forces spokesman, Abolfazl Shekarchi, told state television that Iran had not carried out any “military or offensive operations” in the region and suggested it was a manoeuvre by Israel and the US to blame Iran. On the same day, an attack on the Jazan refinery in southern Saudi Arabia killed a Nepalese worker and started a fire; the Saudi-led coalition blamed Yemen's Houthis, according to the official Saudi news agency, quoted by Gulf News.

The context: the US is maintaining a naval blockade of Iranian ports and talks with Tehran have stalled, despite a memorandum of understanding signed in June, according to ABC News. The exchanges of attacks continue, though less intensely than at the start of the war.

verificacao.nota: Attack, number of victims and nationalities confirmed by ABC News (which quotes Kuwait's army and Ministry of Defence) and by Gulf News, both from 26 Nov. The identification of the employer (Rheinmetall Italia) comes from Italy's Foreign Ministry, quoted only by Gulf News; von der Leyen's reaction is also only in Gulf News. Iranian responsibility is an accusation by Kuwait; there is no independent verification, and Iran denies it. The exact type of facility hit was not disclosed (Gulf News mentions an air defence system). We did not open Italian sources. noticias.titulo: Zelensky criticises Trump for calling Putin a “friend” and says the lack of Patriot missiles is costing lives
noticias.estado: Zelensky's statements to the BBC · Trump defends relationship with Putin · negotiations due to resume in December (expected)
texto: Volodymyr Zelensky did not like seeing Donald Trump call Vladimir Putin a “friend”. In an interview with the BBC recorded in Kyiv and released on Thursday 26 November, the Ukrainian President said this was “strange” and that Putin, whom he called an aggressor and a murderer, “cannot be a friend”, according to the Kyiv Post and Newsweek. He compared the situation to someone having said, during the Second World War, that Hitler was a “good friend”.

It all started with a post by Trump on Truth Social: a photograph of him with Putin, captioned “My Friend”, days after the summit with Putin and Xi Jinping in Shenzhen, China, which ended without a ceasefire in Ukraine. Asked by journalists, Trump replied that he could say Putin “is not a friend”, but that he wants “to make a deal”, and that the closeness is deliberate, according to Newsweek. He also said Putin could attend the G20 summit the US is hosting in Florida next month, if he wishes.

Zelensky again complained about the delay in delivering 48 Patriot air defence missiles, already paid for by allies, which are still waiting for the signature of the US Secretary of Defense, Pete Hegseth. “The lack of these missiles means people's lives,” he said. Ukraine is struggling to stop Russian ballistic missiles, according to the Kyiv Post.

On peace, Zelensky admitted that the latest round of US-mediated talks in Abu Dhabi brought no visible progress and that Russia has returned to maximalist demands. Negotiations are due to resume in December, with no date set and no guarantee that the Europeans will take part.

verificacao.nota: Zelensky's statements to the BBC confirmed in the Kyiv Post and Newsweek (27 Nov), which quote the interview; we did not see the original BBC interview. The Hitler remark is quoted by Newsweek; the Kyiv Post paraphrases it. Trump's reply to journalists and the caption of the post come from Newsweek; the G20 invitation appears in both. The Patriot issue and the Abu Dhabi talks are in both. The White House did not respond to Newsweek. The exact date of the G20 summit was not confirmed.

fontes.nome: Kyiv Post – “Zelensky Draws Hitler Parallel Over Trump’s Friendship With Putin” (27 Nov)

noticias.titulo: New Zealand: final count strips Luxon's government of its majority, and a small centrist party now decides who governs
noticias.estado: Official results released on 27 Nov (fact) · negotiations yet to begin · a fresh election is not ruled out
texto: Three weeks after New Zealand's election, the final count has produced a hung parliament. The official results, released by the Electoral Commission on Friday 27 November, leave the coalition of the prime minister, Christopher Luxon, with 65 of the 130 seats, one short of what it needs, according to Australia's ABC and 1News. On election night, 7 November, the coalition had a majority of two seats.

What changed? Around 400,000 special votes were counted (postal votes, votes from abroad and votes cast outside the voter's own area). Luxon's National Party lost two MPs and is left with 40. Labour has 36 and the Greens a record 17. Three electorates changed hands, two of them by fewer than 200 votes.

The kingmaker now is Opportunity, a centrist party with seven MPs, led by Qiulae Wong. Luxon, who had previously ruled out working with this party, changed his position and said he was “confident” of forming a stable government, with no rush: “it will take as long as it takes”, according to 1News. Wong says she will talk to the National Party first and is open to a deal in which her party abstains on votes; one of her demands is that Winston Peters, of NZ First, should not be foreign minister. The left-wing bloc has no way of getting into power.

Requests for recounts can be made until Wednesday; if there are none, MPs will be declared elected on Thursday 3 December. A constitutional expert quoted by 1News thinks a government before Christmas is unlikely, and hardly anyone rules out a return to the polls.

verificacao.nota: Seat distribution, loss of the majority and Opportunity's role confirmed by ABC (Australia) and 1News (New Zealand), both from 27 Nov. The statements by Luxon and Wong, the electorates that changed hands, the recount deadlines and the date of 3 December come only from 1News. RNZ's headline (“Coalition loses majority, another election possible”) appeared in search results, but the page could not be opened. We did not check the Electoral Commission's website.

fontes.nome: ABC News (Australia) – “New Zealand's incumbent government fails to secure majority from election result” (27 Nov)
1News – “'Unprecedented' election delivers a tough deal for Luxon to seal” (27 Nov)

noticias.titulo: Budget war: Montenegro says he will not go to the Constitutional Court, Ventura dares him to call a confidence vote, and the debate is set for 3 December
noticias.estado: Urgent debate scheduled for 3 Dec · Government says it will not go to the Constitutional Court · confidence vote is only a challenge from Chega
texto: Portugal's 2027 State Budget has been approved, but the argument over what is actually in it goes on. On Thursday 26 November, the prime minister, Luís Montenegro, said from Brussels that the Government has “no intention” of asking the Constitutional Court (TC) to review the measures passed by the opposition, such as zero VAT on a basket of foods. Chega, André Ventura's right-wing populist party, responded by requesting an urgent debate in Parliament, scheduled for 3 December, and dared Montenegro to put forward a motion of confidence.

It all began with Montenegro's interview with RTP, the public broadcaster, on Wednesday night. The prime minister said that provisions such as zero VAT and the increase in the income tax (IRS) rate on rental income are “recommendations” and that Parliament cannot force the Government to legislate. Ventura accused him of an “authoritarian spirit” and pointed out that “Parliament does not make recommendations”. Chega says it will present its own bill for zero VAT and will oppose the final version of the text if it does not include the list of goods covered. The parliamentary leader of the PSD (Montenegro's centre-right party), Hugo Soares, ruled out a confidence motion.

The Socialist Party (PS) is also critical of the Government, but rejects a political crisis. Its secretary-general, José Luís Carneiro, spoke of a “settling of scores” with Parliament, and its parliamentary leader, Eurico Brilhante Dias, promised that “there will be no political crisis”. The President of the Republic, António José Seguro, asked the Government and Parliament to resolve their “differences of interpretation” and, for now, rules out going to the TC: he does not want to “put the cart before the horse”.

What now? Parliament's services have until 9 December to finalise the wording, which may only include changes of form, not of substance. Once he receives the bill, the President has eight days to ask the TC for a preventive review, which can take up to 25 days. He can also sign it into law and request a subsequent review of some provisions, in which case the Budget comes into force immediately. Constitutional experts interviewed by RTP say the final word should belong to the TC and not to a decision by the Government.

verificacao.nota: Montenegro's assurance about the TC comes from Rádio Observador's 22:00 news bulletin on 26 Nov. noticias.titulo: High-speed rail: consortium of Spain's Sacyr and DST confirmed for the Oiã–Soure section, for €2,038 million; Mota-Engil's bid stays out
noticias.estado: Jury's final report confirms winner · contract award expected in December · contract signing expected in 2027
texto: We now know who will build the second section of the high-speed line between Porto and Lisbon. The jury's final report, made public on Thursday 26 November, confirms the win for the consortium led by Spain's Sacyr, together with the Portuguese firms DST and Alberto Couto Alves. The section runs from Oiã (Oliveira do Bairro) to Soure and is about 60 kilometres long, in practice reaching Taveiro, near Coimbra. The winning bid is €2,038 million for design and construction, according to the Portugal Ferroviário website.

The rival consortium, Lusolav, led by Mota-Engil, remains excluded. According to Portugal Ferroviário, the jury found that its bid did not meet the tender specifications: it left out, for example, the connection at Taveiro, the new Coimbra station and parts of the adaptation of the Linha do Norte (the main north–south line), and strayed 400 metres from the corridor approved in the environmental assessment. The excluded bid was about €262 million more expensive.

What comes next? According to ECO, the contract should be awarded next month, signing is expected in June and construction will only begin in 2028. Before that, the consortium must produce the detailed design and prove that it meets the environmental conditions. The third section, between Taveiro and Carregado, the largest of all, is due to be contracted in 2027.

noticias.titulo: Black Friday with prices that went up before coming down: Deco finds fake discounts in several shops and calls for more inspections
noticias.estado: DECO PROteste analysis published · complaints and requests to the Government and ASAE · shops were not contacted
texto: Today is Black Friday, and not all discounts are what they seem. DECO PROteste, Portugal's consumer association, analysed prices at nine chains, both physical and online shops, and found products on promotion that were more expensive than they had been a few days earlier. The consumer rights association has asked ASAE (the Food and Economic Safety Authority, Portugal's food and trading standards regulator) to inspect and punish these practices.

The examples are concrete. According to the analysis published on Thursday, a gaming computer was priced at €1,899 at FNAC during the campaign, when it had cost €1,549.99 until 1 November. A fridge at El Corte Inglés went up by €350 compared with its price a week earlier. Another common trick is to compare with the RRP, the supplier's recommended retail price, which the shop has often never actually charged.

What does the law say? Since 2022, a discount can only be advertised against the lowest price charged by the same shop in the previous 30 days, and that price must be shown. Deco says the infringements have been repeated for years and are now harder to spot, with campaigns lasting weeks, small print in television adverts and fake shops created with the help of artificial intelligence (AI).

The advice: check the price history before buying, be wary of very large discounts and of comparisons with the RRP, compare several shops and keep the receipt. For online purchases there are, as a rule, 14 days to cancel without giving a reason.

texto: Porto Metro's train drivers are on strike today, Friday 27 November, and the network is only partly running. According to the company, there are trains only on the shared trunk section, between Senhora da Hora and Estádio do Dragão, and on the Yellow Line, between Hospital de São João and Santo Ovídio. The other routes, such as those to Póvoa de Varzim and Vila do Conde, have no metro service.

On the two stretches that are running, trains run every 15 minutes between 07:00 and 20:00 and every 30 minutes for the rest of the day, until midnight. The strike was called by SMAQ, the National Union of Portuguese Railway Train Drivers. The workers are demanding that lost purchasing power be restored, better rosters and rest times, and better facilities. Via Porto, part of the Barraqueiro group, which operates and maintains the network, warned that operations could be “prevented on most lines”.

At CP, Portugal's national rail operator, it is also the last day of the train drivers' strike, which began on Monday, this time with a partial stoppage. On Thursday, by 08:00, CP had cancelled 93 of the 247 scheduled trains, including all long-distance services. Anyone with a ticket for a cancelled train can ask for a full refund or exchange it free of charge.

noticias.titulo: European telescope Euclid beats its own record and finds the oldest quasar ever, with a black hole of 360 million suns
noticias.estado: Discovery published in Astronomy & Astrophysics on 24 Nov · mass measured by the James Webb telescope
texto: The European Space Agency's (ESA) Euclid space telescope has found the most distant — and therefore oldest — quasar ever confirmed. It is called J1504+6252 and we see it as it was about 630 million years after the Big Bang. The study was published on Tuesday 24 November in the journal Astronomy & Astrophysics, and beats the previous record, also held by Euclid, by about 40 million years.

A quasar is the very bright centre of a young galaxy, powered by a giant black hole swallowing the gas around it. This one has a mass about 360 million times that of the Sun, calculated with the James Webb telescope. In other words, a monster like this already existed when the Universe was less than 5% of its current age — and explaining how it grew so quickly is a puzzle for astronomers, according to Space.com.

How was it found? Euclid, launched in 2023 to map “dark matter” and “dark energy”, spotted it among millions of objects in 18 months of data. This was followed by observations with the Keck and LBT (Large Binocular Telescope) observatories in the US, and with the Hubble and Webb telescopes. It is the first confirmed quasar with a redshift above 8 (8.13), the measure astronomers use for distance, says Universe Today.
The team, led by Julien Wolf of the Max Planck Institute for Astronomy in Germany, nicknamed it Dún Aonghasa, after a prehistoric Irish fort.

noticias.titulo: Gaia opens its “treasure chest” on Wednesday: the largest star catalogue ever arrives with 2 billion objects and 40 times more data
noticias.estado: Release announced by ESA for 2 Dec, around 11:00 Lisbon time · content described by ESA ahead of publication
texto: It's official: the European Space Agency (ESA) will publish the Gaia mission's fourth major catalogue, the most precise map of the Milky Way, next Wednesday, 2 December. The release is expected at around 11:00 Lisbon time (12:00 Central European Time), ESA announced on Thursday. It will contain about 2 billion stars and other objects with high-quality measurements, selected from nearly 2.8 billion processed.

It is a big leap. The new catalogue, known as DR4, brings together 66 months of observations, between July 2014 and January 2020 — almost double the 34 months of the previous one, from 2022. That amounts to about 400 terabytes, against 10 for DR3. Most of it is the individual measurements of each star over time: the positions alone add up to more than 129 billion records.

Why does this matter? Seeing how a star moves or changes brightness over the years makes it possible to discover what is around it: planets, companion stars, neutron stars or black holes, explains Lund University in Sweden, which takes part in the mission. The list includes, for example, 1,007 possible transits of planets in front of their stars — candidates, not confirmed planets.

Gaia, launched in 2013, finished its observations at the start of 2025. The data now being published had already been collected and were processed over years by hundreds of European scientists. The final catalogue, covering the full mission, is only expected in a few years' time.

cultura.titulo: «As Novas Desventuras de Cliff Booth» (The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth): Brad Pitt is Tarantino's character again, now in David Fincher's hands — and only in IMAX cinemas until it reaches Netflix

ficha.Original title: The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth (2026; USA)
ficha.Director: David Fincher («Seven», «Fight Club», «The Social Network»); screenplay by Quentin Tarantino; cinematography by Erik Messerschmidt; editing by Kirk Baxter
ficha.Cast: Brad Pitt (Cliff Booth), Elizabeth Debicki, Scott Caan, Carla Gugino, Yahya Abdul-Mateen II, Peter Weller; Timothy Olyphant returns
ficha.Release in Portugal: Thursday 26 November 2026, exclusively in IMAX cinemas (distributed by NOS Audiovisuais); around 141 minutes; on Netflix from 23 December
ficha.Reviews: Divided reviews, with more praise than criticism: 85% positive reviews on Rotten Tomatoes (according to MovieWeb, 19 Nov); «Critic's Pick» at The Film Stage (Nick Newman); praise with reservations at Film Stories (Simon Brew); 2.5 out of 4 in a review distributed by news agencies; negative at RogerEbert.com (Brian Tallerico)

texto: Cliff Booth is back. The character who won Brad Pitt the Oscar for best supporting actor in «Once Upon a Time in… Hollywood» (2019) now has a film of his own, written by Quentin Tarantino and directed by David Fincher. «As Novas Desventuras de Cliff Booth» (The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth) opened yesterday, Thursday 26 November, in Portuguese cinemas, but only in IMAX screens: it is a Netflix production, and the platform puts it online on 23 December.

The story is set in 1977, in Los Angeles, eight years after the 2019 film. Cliff is no longer a film stuntman: he works behind the scenes at the studios as a «fixer», the man you call when something goes wrong. It is a sequel that stands on its own. Elizabeth Debicki, Scott Caan, Carla Gugino and Yahya Abdul-Mateen II complete the cast, and Peter Weller plays Cliff's father. With a reported budget of 200 million dollars, it is the most expensive film of both Tarantino's and Fincher's careers.

Its strengths, according to the reviews consulted, lie in the period and the actors. Almost all praise the recreation of 1970s Los Angeles, the soundtrack and, above all, Elizabeth Debicki, singled out as the best thing in the film. Brad Pitt still carries the character with a laid-back charisma, and the scenes with Peter Weller are among the most talked about. Nick Newman, of The Film Stage, sees it as a mature and entertaining work, perhaps the best Fincher in 15 years; Simon Brew, of Film Stories, says it is «mid-range» Fincher but «top-range» Tarantino, and that the director's discipline does the screenwriter good.

Its weaknesses have to do with the story. Several reviews say the film drifts: it is more a portrait of a milieu than a plot, and the main storyline takes a while to get going. Brian Tallerico, of RogerEbert.com, thinks Tarantino's loose style and Fincher's control never meet and goes as far as calling it boring; Stephanie Zacharek, of Time, quoted by MovieWeb, speaks of «a vibe» rather than a film. In short, according to the assessment that emerges from the reviews consulted: an elegant, well-acted period crime film, with 141 minutes that are not always justified — and a rare chance to see a Netflix film on a giant screen.

cultura.titulo: Jimi Hendrix would have turned 84 today: the left-hander from Seattle who played the guitar upside down and changed the sound of rock for ever

ficha.Born and died: 27 November 1942, in Seattle (USA), as Johnny Allen Hendrix; 18 September 1970, in London, aged 27
ficha.Field: Music: electric guitar, rock, blues and psychedelia; songwriter and singer
ficha.Essential work: With the Jimi Hendrix Experience, the albums «Are You Experienced» (1967), «Axis: Bold as Love» (1967–68) and «Electric Ladyland» (1968); songs such as «Hey Joe», «Purple Haze» and «All Along the Watchtower»; performances at Monterey (1967) and Woodstock (1969)
ficha.Recognition: Rock and Roll Hall of Fame (1992); his former home in London, next door to Handel's, is now a museum
ficha.Now: 84 years since his birth on 27 November; the Brook Street flat in London, restored as it was in 1968–69, can be visited at Handel Hendrix House

texto: Jimi Hendrix was born 84 years ago, on 27 November 1942, in Seattle, in the United States. He recorded only three studio albums with his band and died at 27, but few musicians changed rock as much. With the electric guitar, he turned distortion, «feedback» (the amplifier's howl) and the wah-wah pedal into a language of his own, which can still be heard today in almost every guitar band.

The story begins far from the stage. Christened Johnny Allen, he was renamed James Marshall by his father. He got his first guitar, acoustic and second-hand, at around 15. He was left-handed: he turned the guitar upside down and taught himself, copying blues and rock'n'roll records. After a spell in the army as a paratrooper, he spent years as a backing guitarist for names such as Little Richard and the Isley Brothers, until he was discovered in New York by Chas Chandler, of the Animals, who took him to London in 1966.

There, everything sped up. He formed the Jimi Hendrix Experience with Noel Redding and Mitch Mitchell, and the first single, «Hey Joe», made the British charts. In 1967 «Are You Experienced» came out and, in the US, his performance at the Monterey Festival — where he set his guitar on fire — made him a star. «Axis: Bold as Love» and «Electric Ladyland» followed. In August 1969 he closed the Woodstock festival with a version of the American national anthem in which the guitar imitated bombs and bursts of machine-gun fire, in the middle of the Vietnam War. The following year he opened his own studio in New York, Electric Lady. He died a few weeks later, in London, on 18 September 1970, in an episode linked to barbiturates.

A curiosity for anyone passing through London: between 1968 and 1969, Hendrix lived at 23 Brook Street, right next to the house where the Baroque composer Handel had lived two centuries earlier. The two blue plaques sit side by side on the façade. When a journalist mentioned his neighbour, Hendrix admitted he had not known and barely knew Handel's music. Today the two houses form a single museum, and Hendrix's bedroom has been recreated as it was in his day.

cultura.titulo: Did you know that the first people ever photographed were a shoeshiner and his customer, on a Paris street that looked deserted? This autumn, they got a plaque
texto: In 1838, Louis Daguerre pointed his camera from his studio window at the Boulevard du Temple, in Paris. The street was full of people and carts, but in the picture it looks empty. Only two figures remained: a man having his shoes shined and the shoeshiner. They are, as far as is known, the first people to appear in a photograph.

Why only them? Because of the exposure time. The daguerreotype, the technique Daguerre presented to the world in 1839, needed several minutes of light to fix the image on a metal plate. Anyone walking past did not stay in the same spot long enough to leave a mark. The customer, standing with his leg propped up, and the shoeshiner, bent over the shoes, kept still enough to go down in history — without ever knowing it.

The original plate no longer exists as it was. It was given to King Ludwig I of Bavaria and was badly damaged in the bombing of the Second World War. The version that circulates today comes mainly from a copy made in 1937 by Beaumont Newhall, then at the Museum of Modern Art in New York. And Daguerre's studio, next to his theatre of illusions, the Diorama, burned down in 1839.

The most recent part of the story dates from this autumn. Three Swedish filmmakers — Maximilien Van Aertryck, Axel Danielson and Kalle Boman — spent two years in archives, maps and tax records, and commissioned 3D models of the 1838 neighbourhood. Two teams of architects arrived, each on its own, at points a few steps from each other. The spot is next to today's Place de la République, and in October Paris City Council placed a bronze plaque there called «Un détail imprévu» — «an unforeseen detail». Next time you go to Paris, you'll know where to look.

cultura.titulo: Stop: the Porto shopping centre where more than a hundred bands rehearse behind shop windows — and which the City Council now wants to make an official home for music

ficha.Origins: A former 1950s garage, converted into a shopping centre in 1982; as trade declined, the shops were gradually taken over by musicians as rehearsal rooms
ficha.Field: Music: rehearsal rooms, studios and a community of bands of many genres, from rock to metal and blues
ficha.Participants: More than 100 bands and 400 to 500 musicians; the associations ACM – Associação Cultural de Músicos do Stop and Alma Stop, and the informal movement Stop Manifesta
ficha.Now: Listed as a monument of municipal interest (July 2025); in October Porto City Council announced a pre-agreement with NOS to buy the two former cinemas; a bid to have its musical use recognised as intangible cultural heritage is being prepared

texto: On Rua do Heroísmo, in Porto, there is a shopping centre where almost nothing is sold — but where a lot of rehearsing goes on. At Stop, the former shops are now rehearsal rooms for more than 100 bands and 400 to 500 musicians, according to the City Council and the local press. In October, the council announced a pre-agreement with NOS, the telecoms and cinema company, to buy the building's two cinemas and turn them into creative spaces for musicians.

The building was a garage in the 1950s and became a shopping centre in 1982. Over time, the shops moved out and the bands moved in, one unit at a time. The result is a rare case: an entire building of rehearsal rooms, with people from very different genres, from rock and metal to blues, crossing paths in the corridors and the café. Some musicians are organised in associations, such as ACM – Associação Cultural de Músicos do Stop and Alma Stop, and there is an informal movement, Stop Manifesta, which was born in 2023.

That was the year of the scare. In July 2023, the Municipal Police sealed most of the shops for lack of occupancy licences, and hundreds of musicians and shopkeepers were left without a space. There were protests outside the City Council and petitions, and the rooms reopened about two weeks later. Since then, Stop has gone from problem to heritage: it was listed as a monument of municipal interest in July 2025, and the council began a bid to have its musical use recognised as national intangible cultural heritage, in a study by the University of Porto and Lusíada University.

Not everything is simple. According to a JN report in August, rents have gone up — some rooms that cost 100 to 150 euros a month now cost 250, plus electricity — and many bands already share a room. Some fear gentrification. But the community keeps moving: this summer, nine Stop bands gave free concerts in the city's bandstands, in a series organised by the musicians' association with the municipal company Ágora. And the former cinemas, with around 240 and 120 seats, could become the stage that was missing, if the deal and the safety measures are finalised.
